requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to show the edits a review made to requirements outside its group in the same way as {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.mechanical` requires. It MUST also direct them to list every `{example}` a review added and to say that each one needs a test.
rationale:
structural: Every clause of `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.outside` specifies what the skill's text must tell agents. Those clauses are "MUST direct agents to show the edits a review made to requirements outside its group in the same way" and "list every `{example}` a review added and ... say that each one needs a test". None of them prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. They are content obligations, so no structural obligation needs `{impl}` evidence. An alternative wording or placement of the same directions would satisfy the text equally.

The root `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` does carry the directions anyway. Its `section[Habeas%20requirements]/section[Workflow]` paragraph says: "Show the edits reviewers made outside their group the same way, and list added `{example}`s, which each need a test." The preceding sentences define "the same way" as a diff plus a "Mechanical:" list for already-agreed or user-supplied text. The text also says not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. Whether the wording is adequate is a behavioral question, so I left it out of this structural review.

behavioral: The subject `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.outside` imposes three obligations on the `habeas-requirements` skill text. It must direct agents to show edits made outside the group in the same way as `present.mechanical` requires (a diff, then a list of mechanical changes). It must direct them to list every added `{example}`. It must direct them to say each one needs a test.

The test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_shows_edits_outside_a_group_and_added_examples]` calls `assert_in_order` on `habeas-requirements`. That helper reads the bundled skill text and checks that the phrases appear in order.

The test asserts two phrases:
1. `as a diff against that text, then a "Mechanical:" list`. This is the convention from the cited `present.mechanical`. It is the baseline the outside-group instruction refers back to.
2. `Show the edits reviewers made outside their group the same way, and list added `{example}`s, which each need a test`. This covers all three obligations: the same-way instruction, listing added examples, and the need for a test for each.

Both phrases appear in that order in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, workflow step 4. A skill-text obligation is checked by asserting that the directive text is present. Dropping or rewording any of the three directives, or putting the outside-group directive before the convention it refers to, would fail the test.

I found no gap. The obligations of `present.mechanical` itself are covered by its own tests and are not reassessed here.

text: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to show the edits a review made to requirements outside its group in the same way as {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.present.mechanical` requires. It MUST also direct them to list every `{example}` a review added and to say that each one needs a test.

The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. For text that was already agreed or that the user supplied, it MUST direct agents to show the change as a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.
